quickSummary: Seeds consist of a seed coat and embryo. Monocot grass seeds (Zea mays) have a single cotyledon (Scutellum), a proteinaceous Aleurone layer, and protective sheaths: Coleoptile (plumule) and Coleorhiza (radicle). Most dicots are non-endospermic (Gram, Pea; exception: Castor); most monocots are endospermic (Maize; exception: Orchids).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Coleoptile protects the Plumule; Coleorhiza protects the Radicle; Scutellum is the shield-shaped single cotyledon; Aleurone layer is a protein-rich outer endosperm boundary.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MONOCOTYLEDONOUS SEED ARCHITECTURE (*Zea mays*)
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
  PROTECTIVE LAYERS           STORAGE REGION              EMBRYONAL AXIS
 ├── Fused Seed Coat + Pericarp├── Starch-Rich Endosperm   ├── Shield Cotyledon (*Scutellum*)
 └── Protein Aleurone Layer   └── Triploid Storage Tissue ├── Plumule Sheath (*Coleoptile*)
                                                           └── Radicle Sheath (*Coleorhiza*)
conceptBreakdown.content: In cereal grains (*Zea mays*, *Wheat*), the seed coat is membranous and completely fused with the fruit wall (**Pericarp**). The grain is divided into a bulky starch-rich **Endosperm** and a smaller lateral **Embryo**, separated by a specialized proteinaceous **Aleurone Layer**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Dicot vs. Monocot Seed Comparative Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: Dicot vs. Monocot Seed Comparative Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Parameter | Dicotyledonous Seed (*Gram*, *Pea*, *Bean*) | Monocotyledonous Seed (*Maize*, *Wheat*) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cotyledons** | Two fleshy, food-storing cotyledons | Single, thin, shield-shaped cotyledon (**Scutellum**) |
| **Endosperm Status** | Mostly **Non-endospermic / Exalbuminous** (consumed during embryo development; *Exceptions: Castor, Cotton*) | Mostly **Endospermic / Albuminous** (*Exceptions: Orchids, Pothos*) |
| **Protective Sheaths** | Absent over plumule and radicle | **Coleoptile** covers Plumule; **Coleorhiza** covers Radicle |
| **Outer Coat** | Distinct **Testa** (outer) and **Tegmen** (inner) | Seed coat fused completely with fruit wall (**Pericarp**) |
